text:
pagerduty-bot: URGENT: High error rate detected in apac1d - ALB target 5xx spike (P1). More than 1.2k errors in last 5m. Paging on-call.

sam: Seeing the alerts. apac1d ALB target group 1 -> 5xx surge. Metrics: request_5xx ~ 14%, latency up. Customers are reporting errors.

sam: quick check: ALB backend 10.0.22.* target group health shows healthy but request_count spikes and envoys return 502/504.

leo: I’m pulling envoy logs from ingress pods in apac1d. Getting a lot of `connection reset by peer` around TCP keepalive expiry.

jamie: @sam @leo which tier — hosted or dedicated? Could be kernel keepalive changes on nodes after last kernel patch.

sam: Majority are hosted tenants hitting our apac1d fleet. I can confirm a rolling kernel update batch started ~30m ago in that AZ.

leo: Logs snippet from ingress pod (tail):
```
[2026-03-15T01:12:03Z] envoy upstream reset: connection_closed remote_close
[2026-03-15T01:12:04Z] envoy connection idle timeout, closing upstream
[2026-03-15T01:12:05Z] socket: peer reset while sending
```

maria: If kernel keepalive tunables changed, kernel-level timeouts could be shorter than ALB idle timeout -> half-closed sockets and RSTs. ALB keeps connection open, envoy tries to reuse and hits RSTs.

ingress-bot: Detected mismatch: ALB idle timeout=60s, node TCP keepalive interval=30s in apac1d according to recent config push.

sam: Ok actionable plan: 1) Increase ALB idle timeout to 180s for affected target group. 2) Bump envoy connection_idle_timeout to 120s in the ingress config. 3) Roll ingress pods in apac1d gradually (maxUnavailable 1) to pick up new config. 4) If not improving, shift weighted DNS to eu region for critical requests.

leo: I can patch the ingress config now (ConfigMap: `ingress-envoy-timeouts`) and trigger a rolling restart. Applying to apac1d only.

jamie: I'll update ALB target-group attribute: `idle_timeout.timeout_seconds=180`. Running Terraform change now (plan -> apply).

ops-lead: Make sure we annotate the rollout in the incident timeline. Keep me posted on customer impact.

sam: Customer impact: error pages for some customers, roughly 10% of APAC requests failing intermittently. Critical flux for low-latency endpoints.

leo: Patching ingress config: `kubectl -n ingress-system set env deployment/ingress-controller CONNECTION_IDLE=120` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller -n ingress-system`. Doing a canary restart across nodes with label apac1d.

jamie: ALB change applied: idle timeout -> 180s. Propagation in progress.

sam: After ALB change, seeing a small drop in 5xx, but still intermittent resets.

leo: Restarting first batch of ingress pods (3/12). Monitoring.

maria: I'll open a healthcheck override on Route53 for apac1d services to reduce traffic while we stabilize. We can shift 30% traffic to euc1 via weighted record if needed.

ingress-bot: First batch restart completed. Post-restart logs show fewer idle-close events for those pods.

sam: Good. Metrics: request_5xx down from 14% -> 6% in last 2m. Latency stable.

leo: Rolling restarts continue (6/12). No pods failing readiness.

jamie: Noted a config drift in cloud-init on one node in apac1d: `/etc/sysctl.d/99-tcp.conf` was set to `tcp_keepalive_time=30` while baseline is 120. I'm opening an infra ticket to reconcile.

ops-lead: Start drafting customer comms? We should state partial degradation in apac region and that mitigation in progress.

sam: Drafting quick note: "We're investigating elevated errors for APAC customers. Mitigations applied; traffic moving to healthy pods. We'll follow up with root cause once confirmed." + short ETA 30-60m.

maria: I'm going to shift weight 20% to euc1 now to relieve pressure while we finish restart. Applying weighted DNS change.

ingress-bot: Weighted DNS change applied: apac1d -> 80%, euc1 -> 20%. Prop TTL respected (60s).

sam: After weighted shift, 5xx down to ~2% overall. Sounds like we mitigated immediate customer impact.

leo: Rolling restart finished (12/12). No regressions. Kernel config ticket assigned to infra: TICKET-APAC1D-KP-482.

jamie: Can we get a snapshot of connection states on ALB targets? Running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <tg>` shows targets healthy, but connection counts dropping quicker than before.

maria: I'll keep DNS at 80/20 for next 20m and then evaluate returning to normal if stable.

ops-lead: Good work. Start timeline and postmortem skeleton. Make sure to capture the kernel tunable drift and the delayed config push.

sam: Adding timeline to incident doc, will include commands executed and exact timestamps.

maria: Handoff to on-call night shift (leo) at 02:05Z. I'll remain available for escalation. Current status: degraded -> mitigated (partial). Customer impact: reduced to ~2% errors; major endpoints healthy.

leo: Acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor apac for next 2h and escalate if errors creep back up.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged: responder=leo. Pager cleared for primary alerts.

ops-lead: Leave postmortem notes and assign action items: (1) reconcile sysctl baseline across fleet; (2) add ALB <-> envoy keepalive doc; (3) add automated check to detect keepalive drift.

sam: Noted. Will add owners and due dates.

leo: Quick commands used in thread for audit:
```
kubectl -n ingress-system set env deployment/ingress-controller CONNECTION_IDLE=120
kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller -n ingress-system
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn <tg> --attributes Key=idle_timeout.timeout_seconds,Value=180
# Route53 weighted record update via terraform apply
```

sam: Closing note: Keepalive mismatch + kernel config drift triggered reuse of half-closed sockets, producing RSTs and 5xx. Fix: align OS tunables and proxy timeouts; ALB idle timeout increase bought time for rolling restarts.

sam: Incident status: mitigated -> investigating root cause (postmortem in progress).

maria: Thanks team. Handoff complete.

leo: Monitoring...
